```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(scMEGA)
```

scMEGA constructs gene regulatory network predictions from single-cell multiomic
data. This short example executes paired-object construction using synthetic
counts. It checks cell identity and count preservation; it does not infer cell
matches, establish a biological trajectory, or validate a biological network.

The complete scientific workflows remain available as website articles:
[myofibroblast differentiation](https://costalab.github.io/scMEGA/articles/myofibroblast-GRN.html),
[cardiomyocyte remodeling](https://costalab.github.io/scMEGA/articles/cardiomyocyte-GRN.html),
and [PBMC multiome analysis](https://costalab.github.io/scMEGA/articles/pbmc_10x_multiome.html).
Those articles require external datasets and additional reference packages; their
unchanged sources are in `vignettes/articles/` in the repository. Building this
package vignette does not execute those external analyses.

## Synthetic inputs

Use original RNA and ATAC counts, with meaningful feature and cell identifiers.
The ATAC object deliberately stores cells in the opposite order. Twelve cells
ensure that both synthetic peaks meet the existing `min.cells = 10` filter in
`CreatePairedObject()`.

```{r counts}
cells <- paste0("cell", seq_len(12))
rna.counts <- Matrix::Matrix(matrix(seq_len(36), nrow = 3,
  dimnames = list(c("GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC"), cells)), sparse = TRUE)
atac.counts <- Matrix::Matrix(matrix(101:124, nrow = 2,
  dimnames = list(c("chr1-100-200", "chr2-300-400"), cells)), sparse = TRUE)
obj.rna <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  SeuratObject::CreateAssay5Object(counts = rna.counts), assay = "RNA")
obj.atac <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  SeuratObject::CreateAssay5Object(counts = atac.counts[, rev(cells)]), assay = "ATAC")
obj.rna$source_cell <- cells
```

## Declare the pairs

Each row maps an RNA cell and an ATAC cell to a unique output name. The modalities
may use different barcode conventions in real data; their correspondence is
specified by this table, not inferred from matrix position.

```{r construct}
df.pair <- data.frame(RNA = rev(cells), ATAC = rev(cells),
  cell_name = paste0("pair", seq_along(cells)))
paired <- CreatePairedObject(
  df.pair = df.pair,
  obj.coembed = obj.rna,
  obj.rna = obj.rna,
  obj.atac = obj.atac,
  rna.assay = "RNA",
  atac.assay = "ATAC"
)
```

Here `obj.rna` also supplies the RNA metadata as a minimal stand-in for the
coembedding object. In an unpaired-data workflow, supply the actual `CoembedData()`
result through `obj.coembed`, and retain the original count objects separately.

## Verify correspondence

These checks run when the vignette is built and checked.

```{r invariants}
expected.rna <- rna.counts[, df.pair$RNA, drop = FALSE]
expected.atac <- atac.counts[, df.pair$ATAC, drop = FALSE]
colnames(expected.rna) <- colnames(expected.atac) <- df.pair$cell_name
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(paired), df.pair$cell_name),
  identical(as.matrix(SeuratObject::LayerData(paired, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")),
    as.matrix(expected.rna)),
  identical(as.matrix(SeuratObject::LayerData(paired, assay = "ATAC", layer = "counts")),
    as.matrix(expected.atac)),
  identical(unname(paired$source_cell), df.pair$RNA),
  inherits(paired[["ATAC"]], "ChromatinAssay")
)
paired
```

For downstream analysis, use the intended reference assembly and consistent gene,
peak, and motif identifiers. Consult the scientific articles for their assumptions
and data requirements; a valid paired object alone does not establish regulatory
relationships.
